content: Breast diseases can be categorized into two primary groups: those involving disorders of the integumentary system (skin and related structures) and those associated with the reproductive system. The majority of breast diseases are benign and noncancerous in nature. Breast pain, also known as mastalgia, is a common symptom that may or may not be associated with underlying pathology. Infections and inflammations of the breast can arise due to various causes, including physical trauma, milk stasis or engorgement, hormonal stimulation, bacterial or fungal infections, and autoimmune reactions. If infections or inflammations occur repeatedly and are unrelated to lactation, a thorough endocrinological evaluation is necessary to identify potential underlying hormonal or systemic causes.
